description: OPEN INPUT of CARDFILE fails, which is open 4 of the six at :157-162. The paragraph displays its own literal, renders the failing file's own status through Z-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS and abends with RETURN-CODE 12, so the loop never runs, no record is read, no CLOSE paragraph is reached and the end banner at :195 is never displayed - four lines in total. This one is the card file, whose open is reported by CardRepository as a CICS response because its other seventeen callers are online programs. DFHRESP(NOTFND) translates to batch FILE STATUS '23', so the rendered line is 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN0023' - a status this program's open ladder treats like any other non-'00' value, since :255 tests for '00' and nothing else. Statement by statement, the arm pinned is 0300-CARDFILE-OPEN at app/cbl/CBTRN01C.cbl:307-323. :308 moves 8 into APPL-RESULT before the verb runs - the assumed-failure seed, so a file that never reports at all is treated as a failure rather than as a success - :309 issues OPEN INPUT CARD-FILE, and :310 tests CARDFILE-STATUS against '00' and against nothing else. '23' is not '00', so the ELSE at :312 moves 12 into APPL-RESULT at :313, the 88 APPL-AOK condition declared at :143 is false, and the ELSE at :317 runs the four statements that end the run: :318 displays 'ERROR OPENING CARD FILE', :319 moves CARDFILE-STATUS - the failing file's own status field, not another's - into IO-STATUS, :320 performs Z-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS and :321 performs Z-ABEND-PROGRAM. Z-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS at :476-489 takes its ELSE arm because '23' is numeric and IO-STAT1 is not '9': :485 moves '0000' into IO-STATUS-04 and :486 overlays the status at (3:2), so the rendered line is 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN0023' and not 'NNNN2300' or 'NNNN23'. One citation in the retained wording above is worth pinning precisely rather than leaving to inference: the ':255' it names is the DAILY TRANSACTION open's own '00' test, quoted there because the six open paragraphs are textually identical apart from the file, the literal and the status field; the card file's corresponding test is the :310 named here. Z-ABEND-PROGRAM at :469-473 displays 'ABENDING PROGRAM', moves 0 into TIMING, moves 999 into ABCODE and calls 'CEE3ABD', which is why expectedReturnCode is 12 and not 0: 12 is what :313 left in APPL-RESULT and what AbendException.RETURN_CODE_IO_ERROR carries. FOUR LINES IN TOTAL, AND THE ABSENCE OF THE FIFTH IS ITSELF AN ASSERTION: the :156 start banner, then those three. The 'END OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBTRN01C' banner at :195 is NOT expected, because the abend at :321 is reached from inside the fourth open and control never returns to MAIN-PARA - so :164's loop never iterates, no daily transaction is ever read, no cross-reference lookup happens, and none of the six CLOSE paragraphs at :188-193 is entered. A translation that unwound the abend and went on to display the closing banner would emit five lines and fail here, which is the point: CALL 'CEE3ABD' does not return. THE WRITES CHANNEL NAMES EXACTLY THREE DATASETS, AND WHICH THREE IS THE SUBTLE PART. CARDFILE is open 4 of the 6 that MAIN-PARA issues at :157-162, so DALYTRAN (:157), CUSTFILE (:158) and XREFFILE (:159) were opened and are asserted to have been reached and written to zero times, each at its own copybook width - 350 from CVTRA06Y, 500 from CVCUS01Y and 50 from CVACT03Y including the FILLER X(14) the fixture omits. CARDFILE itself is NOT among them: its open is the one that failed, so it was never successfully opened and asserting it as reached would claim an open that did not happen. ACCTFILE (:161) and TRANFILE (:162) are absent for the stronger reason that the abend precedes them entirely. Adding a fourth or a sixth entry here fails the case, and so does dropping one of the three. expectedWrites is EMPTY AS A POSITIVE ASSERTION rather than an absence of interest: CBTRN01C contains zero WRITE and zero REWRITE statements and opens all six of its files OPEN INPUT, so posting is not merely absent from this path but impossible on every path. expectedFinalState is empty and no dataset is pinned on the FINAL_STATE channel, because the only dataset seeded is an input file the run never even read - there is no after-state to distinguish from the before-state, and pinning one would assert an empty dataset by accident. normalisations is empty because the 36-to-50 cross-reference pad has nothing to apply to: XREFFILE is opened but never seeded here, since the run abends before any lookup. GATE G16 IS THEREFORE NOT EXERCISED BY THIS CASE and is not claimed below - stating that plainly is worth more than listing a gate the fixture does not reach. jobParameters is empty because CBTRN01C is the migration's ORPHAN: no EXEC PGM=CBTRN01C appears anywhere in app/jcl or app/proc, so there is no PARM for a parameter to come from and the job carries no scheduled trigger (requirement I4, gate G13). WHY THIS ONE OPEN ARRIVES AS A CICS RESPONSE: CARDFILE is reached through CardRepository, whose other callers are the online programs COCRDLIC, COCRDSLC and COCRDUPC, so it reports outcomes as DFHRESP values rather than as two-character batch statuses. DFHRESP(NOTFND) maps to FILE STATUS '23', and CBTRN01C's open ladder is indifferent to the distinction because :310 compares against '00' and nothing else - every other value, whatever its provenance, takes the same ELSE. That indifference is the source property this case pins on the data-access side, and preserving it means NOT adding a status-specific arm the COBOL does not have. PRACTICE B5, QUIRKS PRESERVED EXACTLY AS FOUND. Two independent source properties of this program are reproduced deliberately elsewhere in the twenty and must not be tidied on the strength of this case: the post-end-of-file cross-reference lookup, where :170-172 sit OUTSIDE the IF END-OF-DAILY-TRANS-FILE = 'N' guard that closes at :169 so a run performs recordsRead + 1 lookups always (case01 pins the repeat after one clean record, case06 pins that it reuses the LAST record's stale card, case04 pins the degenerate form over an empty dataset); and 9000-DALYTRAN-CLOSE reporting the WRONG file, where :372-373 displays 'ERROR CLOSING CUSTOMER FILE' and moves CUSTFILE-STATUS into IO-STATUS on the arm reached when closing the DAILY TRANSACTION file fails (case17). Neither is a defect to be corrected here; correcting either would change what this program has always reported and is a parity violation, not a fix. PRACTICE B4 AND RULE R1, TWO DIVERGENCES DOCUMENTED RATHER THAN SILENTLY 'FIXED'. First, the prompt-mandated class name TransactionPostingJob and the source's own 'Function : Post the records from daily transaction file' header both promise posting, and the verified source posts nothing whatsoever; the name is honoured verbatim and the behaviour is taken from the source, and the real POSTTRAN poster is CBTRN02C migrating as TransactionValidationJob (AAP 0.8.4). Second, and specific to this fixture: the build prompt for case14 described a compound run in which the cross-reference miss lands on the LAST daily-transaction record so that the post-end-of-file lookup repeats the miss - thirteen DISPLAY lines, RETURN-CODE 0, three datasets seeded - and named members 'expectedRecords' and a bare list of message strings. CBTRN01CParityTest, authored against this same ParityCase constructor, instead allocates case14 to the CARDFILE open failure at its :1498-1505, calling openFailureCase with case identifier "case14", dataset CARDFILE, literal ERROR_OPENING_CARDFILE and status STATUS_NOT_FOUND. THE TEST CLASS IS FOLLOWED, for three reasons: it is the compiled contract the gate executes; it states explicitly that a shipped fixture set must return the same twenty ParityCase values it builds, so a fixture asserting a different scenario would break the seam that adopts it; and the prompt's scenario is ALREADY COVERED by case01, case04 and case06, so taking case14 for it would have duplicated case06 while leaving the fourth open arm - the only one whose status arrives as a CICS response - unasserted. The named members do not exist on the contract either: there is no 'expectedRecords', writes and final state are separate members, and a message is an object carrying its channel; deserialisation refuses unknown keys, so a fixture written to the prompt's vocabulary could not load at all. Sibling case04.json records the identical prompt-versus-contract divergence and resolves it the same way, so the two fixtures are consistent with each other. PRACTICE B12, BASELINE PROVENANCE. These expected values are STATICALLY DERIVED: read out of app/cbl/CBTRN01C.cbl paragraph by paragraph and cross-checked against the copybook byte layouts in app/cpy (CVTRA06Y 350, CVCUS01Y 500, CVACT03Y 50, CVACT01Y 300), against the absence of any JCL for this program - which is what fixes its parameter list as empty - and against the real ASCII fixtures. They were NEVER captured from, recorded against or replayed from any execution of the legacy COBOL, because executing it is empirically impossible in this environment: there is no z/OS or CICS runtime, the available compiler reports its indexed file handler as disabled, no Language Environment CEE* services exist so the CALL 'CEE3ABD' at :473 cannot be reached at all, the IBM-supplied DFHAID, DFHBMSCA and DFHATTR copybooks are absent from the repository, and app/cpy/CUSTREC.cpy carries literal TAB characters that break parsing outright. AAP 0.7.6 records eight independently verified blockers. The substitution changes the PROVENANCE of the expected values and nothing else - twenty cases, field-for-field diffing and the diff-count-equals-zero gate all stand - and it is escalated for explicit user confirmation as risk R-A rather than silently absorbed. PRACTICE B11, REVIEWABLE DERIVATION, AND PRACTICE B3, REFERENCE INPUTS IMMUTABLE. The single seeded row is app/data/ASCII/dailytran.txt row 1, taken verbatim and never retyped: its DALYTRAN-ID occupies bytes 1-16 ('0000000000683580') and its DALYTRAN-CARD-NUM bytes 263-278 ('4859452612877065') by CVTRA06Y's own offsets, its DALYTRAN-AMT image '0000005047G' carries the zoned sign overpunch that encodes +7 in the final digit, and its trailing FILLER X(20) is present and space-filled so the row measures exactly 350 (gates G19 and G21). Neither dailytran.txt nor any other file under app/data was edited to produce this case - the arm is reached by INJECTING the open response, not by mutating the oracle. PRACTICE B1, NO PLACEHOLDERS: the record appears in full, with no ellipsis, no truncation and no summarised span. PRACTICE B7, DETERMINISM: nothing here reads a wall clock, draws a random value or consults the environment, and CBTRN01C reads no clock either, so the fingerprint is byte-identical on every run. PRACTICE B8, EXPLICIT OVER IMPLICIT: the bytes are US-ASCII, stated and never taken from the platform default; expectedReturnCode is present explicitly as 12 rather than left to a default; every dataset is addressed by its eight-character binding key, so no fully-qualified mainframe dataset name appears anywhere in the fixture (gate G46); and the four expected lines each declare their DISPLAY_LINE channel rather than implying it. review_rules returns exactly one line, "No user rules provided.", and that single line is the whole document, so NO user rule governs this fixture; the binding standard is the enterprise practice set B1-B12, and the absence of project rules is not licence to assert less. Gates carried: G13 (a runnable orphan that nothing triggers and that takes no parameter), G15 (one of the twenty cases this program owns), G18 (the diff count for this case must be zero), G19 and G21 (the 350-, 500- and 50-byte widths, every FILLER present and space-filled), G30 (the :310 status ladder judged in source order, '00' first and every other value second), G35 (the abend carries RETURN-CODE 12), G46 (binding keys only, no dataset name in the fixture), G47 (the '00' outcome at three open call sites followed by the '23' outcome at the fourth) and G51 (the tasklet body is driven directly, with no JobLauncher, no application context and no HTTP layer in the path). G16 is NOT carried, as explained above, because no cross-reference row is seeded. G32 does not apply: CBTRN01C contains zero GO TO statements.
